About: A full-day CVPR 2024 workshop bringing academia and industry together (UCLA, Tübingen, NVIDIA, Waymo, Zoox/MIT, Wayve, Argoverse) on the state of autonomous driving. This report distills the talks with substantive notes.

Three threads ran through the day: open-source simulation & benchmarking to close the academia–industry gap; foundation / vision-language models moving into every layer of the AV stack; and scaling to the long tail with robust, end-to-end autonomy.

03 · Insights

The workshop, talk by talk

A · Simulation & benchmarking
01

An Open-Source Simulation Ecosystem for AV Research

Bolei Zhou · UCLA · MetaDrive / ScenarioNet
The gap to close
  • Academia is limited by hardware/GPU constraints; access to real-world data and simulators bridges the gap to industry
  • AV companies release real-world datasets — but they need a common format
  • An open-source simulator that mimics real-world quality is essential
MetaDrive & ScenarioNet
  • MetaDrive: a lightweight, data-driven simulator
  • ScenarioNet: a large-scale repository built from low-resolution labeled data — 500,000 scenarios so far
  • Users add their own modules; a two-stage method turns noisy, fragmented data into coherent scenarios
Safety & realism
  • Safety-critical scenarios are rare → closed-loop adversarial training adds adversarial scenarios and risk-aware driving
  • Text-to-image VLMs create diverse, high-quality images; simulator-conditioned generation (SimGen) yields realistic scenes
  • Work underway on urban environments for small-robot city simulation
[1] B. Zhou, “Building an Open-Source Simulation Ecosystem for AI and Mobility Research,” CVPR 2024 Workshop on Autonomous Driving.
02

Non-Reactive AV Simulation and Benchmarking

Kashyap Chitta · University of Tübingen · Tübingen AI Center
Why non-reactive sim
  • 75% of driving data is just driving straight; current sims are limited, not very realistic, and GPU-hungry
  • Bypass these constraints with minimal rendering in a 2D bird's-eye-view simulation
The setup
  • The ego vehicle is restricted to its first frame; the whole simulation runs without new sensor data (assume the initial data is complete)
  • The ego vehicle is invisible to other vehicles' sensors — hence ‘non-reactive’
What it measures
  • No collisions · driving-area compliance · time-to-collision
  • Ego progress · comfort of driving — all in a lightweight 2D BEV
[2] K. Chitta, “Non-Reactive Autonomous Vehicle Simulation and Benchmarking,” CVPR 2024 Workshop on Autonomous Driving.
B · Foundation models & scaling
03

Next-Gen AV with Foundation Models

Sanja Fidler · NVIDIA
From rules to end-to-end
  • NVIDIA spans ADAS across hardware, infrastructure, simulation, NVIDIA Drive and research
  • Shift from rule-based systems to AI / end-to-end models, which simplify ADS software
  • Rare cases need rapid processing — slow iteration is not acceptable
Foundation models in the stack
  • Vision-Language Models enable auto-labeling, captioning and clustering; video captions feed later analysis
  • New tools: Picasso (text-to-image), NeMo, ViLA (captioning), DLSS 3.0; the Blackwell GPU adds generative AI
  • FM-powered AV stack: images → trajectory tokens → pretrained backbone → driving stack, benchmarked in simulation
Modeling the long tail
  • Model harsh-weather video from internet video, given the rarity of real accident data
  • Use enough tokens to model small objects (e.g. pillars) without slowing down; dynamic scenes (motorcycles) stay hard
  • A simulation-first approach using neural reconstruction graphics
[3] S. Fidler, “Next-Gen AV with Foundation Models,” CVPR 2024 Workshop on Autonomous Driving.
04

Buckle Up for the Future: Scaling Autonomous Driving

Congcong Li · Waymo
The problem
  • Each year ~50 million injuries and 1.35 million deaths occur on the streets
  • Long-tail handling is the critical challenge for scaling autonomous driving
What Waymo built
  • Multi-modality sensor fusion; mining and augmenting rare examples
  • Auto-labeling plus an efficient ML development ecosystem
  • Next step: leverage the knowledge and reasoning of LLMs / VLMs
UP-VL: label-free 3D perception
  • Human labeling is slow and inaccurate for scaling → focus on a perception database (billions of points and images)
  • UP-VL: unsupervised multi-modal auto-labeling + 3D perception trained with vision-language distillation — no human annotations
  • A hybrid paradigm: combine classic methods with end-to-end approaches
[4] M. Najibi et al., “Unsupervised 3D Perception with 2D Vision-Language Distillation (UP-VL),” CVPR 2024 Workshop on Autonomous Driving.
C · Perception, forecasting & robust autonomy
05

Argoverse Challenges — Scene Flow, Forecasting & Occupancy

Kyle Vedder (Argoverse) · CVPR 2024 Argoverse Challenges
Scene flow
  • Datasets of image, lidar and more; scene flow spans background, vehicles and pedestrians
  • A simple Kalman filter tracked changes between consecutive frames to detect moving objects
Flow4D & clustering
  • Flow4D: early and temporal fusion, fusing lidar and camera information
  • Clustering + ICP: high-quality priors; improved clustering via foreground/background estimation
Forecasting & 4D occupancy
  • End-to-end forecasting: various sensor-fusion methods, but performance issues on the AV stack — ongoing work
  • 4D occupancy forecasting without annotations via an implicit model; parallel processing of large query sets
  • A large receptive field helps find lidar evidence; most foreground motion is in the BEV plane
[5] K. Vedder et al., “Argoverse 2 Challenges: Scene Flow, Forecasting and 4D Occupancy,” CVPR 2024 Workshop on Autonomous Driving.
06

Towards Scalable and Robust Autonomy

Nick Roy · Zoox · MIT
Architecture & end-to-end
  • A general ADS architecture; end-to-end AI can replace individual modules, connecting sensors directly to motors
  • Learned estimators trained with domain knowledge help generate data — but the number of sensors is a challenge
Robustness in the wild
  • Debris is hard to detect and is often mistaken for noise; buses must be perceived and avoided
  • Significant out-of-domain uncertainty is computationally heavy and vulnerable to aliasing
Planning
  • Reinforcement learning is used for the planning module
  • Open question: how to match standard methods with end-to-end approaches
[6] N. Roy, “Towards Scalable and Robust Autonomy,” CVPR 2024 Workshop on Autonomous Driving.
04 · Conclusions

Synthesis across the workshop

Trends

  • Open-source simulators and a common scenario format (MetaDrive / ScenarioNet) are closing the academia–industry gap.
  • Foundation / vision-language models are moving into every layer of the AV stack — labeling, generation, planning.
  • The field is converging on end-to-end, simulation-first development.

Vision

  • Label-free 3D perception at scale (UP-VL) and auto-generated safety-critical scenarios.
  • Realistic generative simulation — harsh weather and accidents — from internet-scale video.
  • Robust autonomy that handles the long tail: debris, rare events, out-of-domain uncertainty.

Implications for us

  • Invest in open simulation, benchmarking and a shared scenario format.
  • Adopt VLM-powered auto-labeling and generative data to cover rare cases cheaply.
  • Treat long-tail robustness and safety validation as first-class, not add-ons.
